body.statement: For every fixed \(n\ge2\), \(k\ge2\), and \(1\le m\le k-1\), there are constants \((c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) and a nonzero interval of \(\delta\) for which every model \(\theta_\delta\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:bounded\text{-}rate\text{-}class\text{-}example}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\). The decoder is nonlinear, degree one, volume preserving, uniformly bi-Lipschitz, and bounded with its inverse in \(C^k\); the mechanisms are positive bounded periodic densities and attain critical order \(m\).
body.justification: The strengthened uniform rate envelopes define a concrete nonempty causal class rather than an oracle regularity shell.
body.gap: Exact-identification results allow broader qualitative classes, while a uniform inverse modulus needs explicit control of oscillation and Jacobian conditioning.
body.consumer: The example calibrates admissible constants for simulations and supplies a baseline family for sharpness constructions.
